title: TagDuel 2v2 Main Deck, Extra Deck and field-zone boundaries
scenarios: A classic four-seat TagDuel accepts 20-card and 30-card Main Decks and one currently enabled Fusion in each active physical Extra Deck. The rule profile fixes three Monster Zones, three Spell/Trap Zones and a separate Field Zone; occupied arrays are asserted not to exceed their three-slot capacities.
The same constructor rejects a 19-card Main Deck and a 31-card Main Deck. A synthetic six-entry Extra Deck input is rejected by the engine's five-card cap before the independent three-copy check.
invariants: Main Deck minimum is 20 and maximum is 30.
Each team has three Monster Zones and three Spell/Trap Zones.
Field Zone remains separate from the three Spell/Trap slots.
Current RULES_PROFILE hand limit remains six.
All four physical participants and card UIDs remain unique.
The rules profile declares an Extra Deck maximum of five and a three-copy limit.
limits: Tests use real compiled TagDuel, rulesProfile and enabled card registry modules.
Main/Extra Deck fixtures use existing enabled cards; no collection or inventory mutation occurs.
No runtime, resolver, catalog manifest, allowlist, persistent database or player data is modified.
This verifies structural rules, not new card behavior.
No live Discord API session is performed.
command: npm run check && npm run build && node --test tests/tagDeckExtraAndZoneBoundaries2v2.test.cjs
limitations: The six-entry negative fixture deliberately repeats the one supported Fusion to reach the length guard; the engine rejects it at the five-card cap before copy-count validation. It is not represented as a legal Deck.

The shared base exposes only one supported Fusion identity (45231177). A valid exactly-five-card Extra Deck cannot be constructed while also respecting the three-copy rule; the positive five-card case is not claimed.

The six-entry negative fixture deliberately repeats the one supported Fusion to reach the length guard; the engine rejects it at the five-card cap before copy-count validation. It is not represented as a legal Deck.
